0: In the beginning of God’s preparing the heavens and the earth—
1: the earth hath existed waste and void, and darkness is on the face of the deep, and the Spirit of God fluttering on the face of the waters,
2: and God saith, ‘Let light be;’ and light is.
3: And God seeth the light that it is good, and God separateth between the light and the darkness,
4: and God calleth to the light ‘Day,’ and to the darkness He hath called ‘Night;’ and there is an evening, and there is a morning—day one.
5: And God saith, ‘Let an expanse be in the midst of the waters, and let it be separating between waters and waters.’
6: And God maketh the expanse, and it separateth between the waters which are under the expanse, and the waters which are above the expanse: and it is so.
7: And God calleth to the expanse ‘Heavens;’ and there is an evening, and there is a morning—day second.
8: And God saith, ‘Let the waters under the heavens be collected unto one place, and let the dry land be seen:’ and it is so.
9: And God calleth to the dry land ‘Earth,’ and to the collection of the waters He hath called ‘Seas;’ and God seeth that it is good.
10: And God saith, ‘Let the earth yield tender grass, herb sowing seed, fruit-tree (whose seed is in itself) making fruit after its kind, on the earth:’ and it is so.
11: And the earth bringeth forth tender grass, herb sowing seed after its kind, and tree making fruit (whose seed is in itself) after its kind; and God seeth that it is good;
12: and there is an evening, and there is a morning—day third.
13: And God saith, ‘Let luminaries be in the expanse of the heavens, to make a separation between the day and the night, then they have been for signs, and for seasons, and for days and years,
14: and they have been for luminaries in the expanse of the heavens to give light upon the earth:’ and it is so.
15: And God maketh the two great luminaries, the great luminary for the rule of the day, and the small luminary—and the stars—for the rule of the night;
16: and God giveth them in the expanse of the heavens to give light upon the earth,
17: and to rule over day and over night, and to make a separation between the light and the darkness; and God seeth that it is good;
18: and there is an evening, and there is a morning—day fourth.
19: And God saith, ‘Let the waters teem with the teeming living creature, and fowl let fly on the earth on the face of the expanse of the heavens.’
20: And God prepareth the great monsters, and every living creature that is creeping, which the waters have teemed with, after their kind, and every fowl with wing, after its kind, and God seeth that it is good.
21: And God blesseth them, saying, ‘Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas, and the fowl let multiply in the earth:’
22: and there is an evening, and there is a morning—day fifth.
23: And God saith, ‘Let the earth bring forth the living creature after its kind, cattle and creeping thing, and beast of the earth after its kind:’ and it is so.
24: And God maketh the beast of the earth after its kind, and the cattle after their kind, and every creeping thing of the ground after its kind, and God seeth that it is good.
25: And God saith, ‘Let Us make man in Our image, according to Our likeness, and let them rule over fish of the sea, and over fowl of the heavens, and over cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that is creeping on the earth.’
26: And God prepareth the man in His image; in the image of God He prepared him, a male and a female He prepared them.
27: And God blesseth them, and God saith to them, ‘Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the earth, and subdue it, and rule over fish of the sea, and over fowl of the heavens, and over every living thing that is creeping upon the earth.’
28: And God saith, ‘Lo, I have given to you every herb sowing seed, which is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree in which is the fruit of a tree sowing seed, to you it is for food;
29: and to every beast of the earth, and to every fowl of the heavens, and to every creeping thing on the earth, in which is breath of life, every green herb is for food:’ and it is so.
30: And God seeth all that He hath done, and lo, very good; and there is an evening, and there is a morning—day the sixth.
31: And the heavens and the earth are completed, and all their host;
32: and God completeth by the seventh day His work which He hath made, and ceaseth by the seventh day from all His work which He hath made.
33: And God blesseth the seventh day, and sanctifieth it, for in it He hath ceased from all His work which God had prepared for making.
34: These are births of the heavens and of the earth in their being prepared, in the day of Jehovah God’s making earth and heavens;
35: and no shrub of the field is yet in the earth, and no herb of the field yet sprouteth, for Jehovah God hath not rained upon the earth, and a man there is not to serve the ground,
36: and a mist goeth up from the earth, and hath watered the whole face of the ground.
37: And Jehovah God formeth the man—dust from the ground, and breatheth into his nostrils breath of life, and the man becometh a living creature.
38: And Jehovah God planteth a garden in Eden, at the east, and He setteth there the man whom He hath formed;
39: and Jehovah God causeth to sprout from the ground every tree desirable for appearance, and good for food, and the tree of life in the midst of the garden, and the tree of knowledge of good and evil.
40: And a river is going out from Eden to water the garden, and from thence it is parted, and hath become four chief rivers;
41: the name of the one is Pison, it is that which is surrounding the whole land of the Havilah where the gold is,
42: and the gold of that land is good, there is the bdolach and the shoham stone;
43: and the name of the second river is Gibon, it is that which is surrounding the whole land of Cush;
44: and the name of the third river is Hiddekel, it is that which is going east of Asshur; and the fourth river is Phrat.
45: And Jehovah God taketh the man, and causeth him to rest in the garden of Eden, to serve it, and to keep it.
46: And Jehovah God layeth a charge on the man, saying, ‘Of every tree of the garden eating thou dost eat;
47: and of the tree of knowledge of good and evil, thou dost not eat of it, for in the day of thine eating of it—dying thou dost die.’
48: And Jehovah God saith, ‘Not good for the man to be alone, I do make to him an helper—as his counterpart.’
49: And Jehovah God formeth from the ground every beast of the field, and every fowl of the heavens, and bringeth in unto the man, to see what he doth call it; and whatever the man calleth a living creature, that is its name.
50: And the man calleth names to all the cattle, and to fowl of the heavens, and to every beast of the field; and to man hath not been found an helper—as his counterpart.
51: And Jehovah God causeth a deep sleep to fall upon the man, and he sleepeth, and He taketh one of his ribs, and closeth up flesh in its stead.
52: And Jehovah God buildeth up the rib which He hath taken out of the man into a woman, and bringeth her in unto the man;
53: and the man saith, ‘This is the proper step! bone of my bone, and flesh of my flesh!’ for this it is called Woman, for from a man hath this been taken;
54: therefore doth a man leave his father and his mother, and hath cleaved unto his wife, and they have become one flesh.
55: And they are both of them naked, the man and his wife, and they are not ashamed of themselves.
56: And the serpent hath been subtile above every beast of the field which Jehovah God hath made, and he saith unto the woman, ‘Is it true that God hath said, Ye do not eat of every tree of the garden?’
57: And the woman saith unto the serpent, ‘Of the fruit of the trees of the garden we do eat,
58: and of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden God hath said, Ye do not eat of it, nor touch it, lest ye die.’
60: for God doth know that in the day of your eating of it—your eyes have been opened, and ye have been as God, knowing good and evil.’
61: And the woman seeth that the tree is good for food, and that it is pleasant to the eyes, and the tree is desirable to make one wise, and she taketh of its fruit and eateth, and giveth also to her husband with her, and he doth eat;
62: and the eyes of them both are opened, and they know that they are naked, and they sew fig-leaves, and make to themselves girdles.
63: And they hear the sound of Jehovah God walking up and down in the garden at the breeze of the day, and the man and his wife hide themselves from the face of Jehovah God in the midst of the trees of the garden.
64: And Jehovah God calleth unto the man, and saith to him, ‘Where art thou?’
65: and he saith, ‘Thy sound I have heard in the garden, and I am afraid, for I am naked, and I hide myself.’
66: And He saith, ‘Who hath declared to thee that thou art naked? of the tree of which I have commanded thee not to eat, hast thou eaten?’
67: and the man saith, ‘The woman whom Thou didst place with me—she hath given to me of the tree—and I do eat.’
68: And Jehovah God saith to the woman, ‘What is this thou hast done?’ and the woman saith, ‘The serpent hath caused me to forget—and I do eat.’
69: And Jehovah God saith unto the serpent, ‘Because thou hast done this, cursed art thou above all the cattle, and above every beast of the field: on thy belly dost thou go, and dust thou dost eat, all days of thy life;
70: and enmity I put between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; he doth bruise thee—the head, and thou dost bruise him—the heel.’
71: Unto the woman He said, ‘Multiplying I multiply thy sorrow and thy conception, in sorrow dost thou bear children, and toward thy husband is thy desire, and he doth rule over thee.’
72: And to the man He said, ‘Because thou hast hearkened to the voice of thy wife, and dost eat of the tree concerning which I have charged thee, saying, Thou dost not eat of it, cursed is the ground on thine account; in sorrow thou dost eat of it all days of thy life,
73: and thorn and bramble it doth bring forth to thee, and thou hast eaten the herb of the field;
74: by the sweat of thy face thou dost eat bread till thy return unto the ground, for out of it hast thou been taken, for dust thou art, and unto dust thou turnest back.’
75: And the man calleth his wife’s name Eve: for she hath been mother of all living.
76: And Jehovah God doth make to the man and to his wife coats of skin, and doth clothe them.
77: And Jehovah God saith, ‘Lo, the man was as one of Us, as to the knowledge of good and evil; and now, lest he send forth his hand, and have taken also of the tree of life, and eaten, and lived to the age,’—
78: Jehovah God sendeth him forth from the garden of Eden to serve the ground from which he hath been taken;
79: yea, he casteth out the man, and causeth to dwell at the east of the garden of Eden the cherubs and the flame of the sword which is turning itself round to guard the way of the tree of life.
80: And the man knew Eve his wife, and she conceiveth and beareth Cain, and saith, ‘I have gotten a man by Jehovah;’
81: and she addeth to bear his brother, even Abel. And Abel is feeding a flock, and Cain hath been servant of the ground.
82: And it cometh to pass at the end of days that Cain bringeth from the fruit of the ground a present to Jehovah;
83: and Abel, he hath brought, he also, from the female firstlings of his flock, even from their fat ones; and Jehovah looketh unto Abel and unto his present,
84: and unto Cain and unto his present He hath not looked; and it is very displeasing to Cain, and his countenance is fallen.
85: And Jehovah saith unto Cain, ‘Why hast thou displeasure? and why hath thy countenance fallen?
86: Is there not, if thou dost well, acceptance? and if thou dost not well, at the opening a sin-offering is crouching, and unto thee its desire, and thou rulest over it.’
87: And Cain saith unto Abel his brother, ‘Let us go into the field;’ and it cometh to pass in their being in the field, that Cain riseth up against Abel his brother, and slayeth him.
88: And Jehovah saith unto Cain, ‘Where is Abel thy brother?’ and he saith, ‘I have not known; my brother’s keeper—I?’
89: And He saith, ‘What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother’s blood is crying unto Me from the ground;
90: and now, cursed art thou from the ground, which hath opened her mouth to receive the blood of thy brother from thy hand;
91: when thou tillest the ground, it doth not add to give its strength to thee—a wanderer, even a trembling one, thou art in the earth.’
92: And Cain saith unto Jehovah, ‘Greater is my punishment than to be borne;
93: lo, Thou hast driven me to-day from off the face of the ground, and from Thy face I am hid; and I have been a wanderer, even a trembling one, in the earth, and it hath been—every one finding me doth slay me.’
94: And Jehovah saith to him, ‘Therefore—of any slayer of Cain sevenfold it is required;’ and Jehovah setteth to Cain a token that none finding him doth slay him.
95: And Cain goeth out from before Jehovah, and dwelleth in the land, moving about east of Eden;
96: and Cain knoweth his wife, and she conceiveth, and beareth Enoch; and he is building a city, and he calleth the name of the city, according to the name of his son—Enoch.
97: And born to Enoch is Irad; and Irad hath begotten Mehujael; and Mehujael hath begotten Methusael; and Methusael hath begotten Lamech.
98: And Lamech taketh to himself two wives, the name of the one Adah, and the name of the second Zillah.
99: And Adah beareth Jabal, he hath been father of those inhabiting tents and purchased possessions;
100: and the name of his brother is Jubal, he hath been father of every one handling harp and organ.
101: And Zillah she also bare Tubal-Cain, an instructor of every artificer in brass and iron; and a sister of Tubal-Cain is Naamah.
102: And Lamech saith to his wives:—‘Adah and Zillah, hear my voice; Wives of Lamech, give ear to my saying: For a man I have slain for my wound, Even a young man for my hurt;
103: For sevenfold is required for Cain, And for Lamech seventy and sevenfold.’
104: And Adam again knoweth his wife, and she beareth a son, and calleth his name Seth, ‘for God hath appointed for me another seed instead of Abel:’ for Cain had slain him.
105: And to Seth, to him also a son hath been born, and he calleth his name Enos; then a beginning was made of preaching in the name of Jehovah.
108: And Adam liveth an hundred and thirty years, and begetteth a son in his likeness, according to his image, and calleth his name Seth.
109: And the days of Adam after his begetting Seth are eight hundred years, and he begetteth sons and daughters.
110: And all the days of Adam which he lived are nine hundred and thirty years, and he dieth.
111: And Seth liveth an hundred and five years, and begetteth Enos.
112: And Seth liveth after his begetting Enos eight hundred and seven years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
113: And all the days of Seth are nine hundred and twelve years, and he dieth.
114: And Enos liveth ninety years, and begetteth Cainan.
115: And Enos liveth after his begetting Cainan eight hundred and fifteen years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
117: And Cainan liveth seventy years, and begetteth Mahalaleel.
118: And Cainan liveth after his begetting Mahalaleel eight hundred and forty years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
119: And all the days of Cainan are nine hundred and ten years, and he dieth.
120: And Mahalaleel liveth five and sixty years, and begetteth Jared.
126: And Enoch liveth five and sixty years, and begetteth Methuselah.
127: And Enoch walketh habitually with God after his begetting Methuselah three hundred years, and begetteth sons and daughters.
130: And Methuselah liveth an hundred and eighty and seven years, and begetteth Lamech.
134: and calleth his name Noah, saying, ‘This one doth comfort us concerning our work, and concerning the labour of our hands, because of the ground which Jehovah hath cursed.’
137: And Noah is a son of five hundred years, and Noah begetteth Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
138: And it cometh to pass that mankind have begun to multiply on the face of the ground, and daughters have been born to them,
139: and sons of God see the daughters of men that they are fair, and they take to themselves women of all whom they have chosen.
140: And Jehovah saith, ‘My Spirit doth not strive in man—to the age; in their erring they are flesh:’ and his days have been an hundred and twenty years.
141: The fallen ones were in the earth in those days, and even afterwards when sons of God come in unto daughters of men, and they have borne to them—they are the heroes, who, from of old, are the men of name.
142: And Jehovah seeth that abundant is the wickedness of man in the earth, and every imagination of the thoughts of his heart only evil all the day;
143: and Jehovah repenteth that He hath made man in the earth, and He grieveth Himself—unto His heart.
144: And Jehovah saith, ‘I wipe away man whom I have prepared from off the face of the ground, from man unto beast, unto creeping thing, and unto fowl of the heavens, for I have repented that I have made them.’
145: And Noah found grace in the eyes of Jehovah.
146: These are births of Noah: Noah is a righteous man; perfect he hath been among his generations; with God hath Noah walked habitually.
148: And the earth is corrupt before God, and the earth is filled with violence.
149: And God seeth the earth, and lo, it hath been corrupted, for all flesh hath corrupted its way on the earth.
150: And God said to Noah, ‘An end of all flesh hath come before Me, for the earth hath been full of violence from their presence; and lo, I am destroying them with the earth.
151: ‘Make for thyself an ark of gopher-wood; rooms dost thou make with the ark, and thou hast covered it within and without with cypress;
152: and this is that which thou dost with it: three hundred cubits is the length of the ark, fifty cubits its breadth, and thirty cubits its height;
153: a window dost thou make for the ark, and unto a cubit thou dost restrain it from above; and the opening of the ark thou dost put in its side,—lower, second, and third stories dost thou make it.
154: And I, lo, I am bringing in the deluge of waters on the earth to destroy all flesh, in which is a living spirit, from under the heavens; all that is in the earth doth expire.
155: ‘And I have established My covenant with thee, and thou hast come in unto the ark, thou, and thy sons, and thy wife, and thy son’s wives with thee;
156: and of all that liveth, of all flesh, two of every sort thou dost bring in unto the ark, to keep alive with thee; male and female are they.
158: ‘And thou, take to thyself of all food that is eaten; and thou hast gathered unto thyself, and it hath been to thee and to them for food.’
160: And Jehovah saith to Noah, ‘Come in, thou and all thy house, unto the ark, for thee I have seen righteous before Me in this generation;
161: of all the clean beasts thou dost take to thee seven pairs, a male and its female; and of the beasts which are not clean two, a male and its female;
163: for after other seven days I am sending rain on the earth forty days and forty nights, and have wiped away all the substance that I have made from off the face of the ground.’
165: and Noah is a son of six hundred years, and the deluge of waters hath been upon the earth.
170: In the six hundredth year of the life of Noah, in the second month, in the seventeenth day of the month, in this day have been broken up all fountains of the great deep, and the net-work of the heavens hath been opened,
171: and the shower is on the earth forty days and forty nights.
172: In this self-same day went in Noah, and Shem, and Ham, and Japheth, sons of Noah, and Noah’s wife and the three wives of his sons with them, unto the ark;
173: they, and every living creature after its kind, and every beast after its kind, and every creeping thing that is creeping on the earth after its kind, and every fowl after its kind, every bird—every wing.
175: and they that are coming in, male and female of all flesh, have come in as God hath commanded him, and Jehovah doth close it for him.
176: And the deluge is forty days on the earth, and the waters multiply, and lift up the ark, and it is raised up from off the earth;
177: and the waters are mighty, and multiply exceedingly upon the earth; and the ark goeth on the face of the waters.
178: And the waters have been very very mighty on the earth, and covered are all the high mountains which are under the whole heavens;
179: fifteen cubits upwards have the waters become mighty, and the mountains are covered;
180: and expire doth all flesh that is moving on the earth, among fowl, and among cattle, and among beasts, and among all the teeming things which are teeming on the earth, and all mankind;
181: all in whose nostrils is breath of a living spirit—of all that is in the dry land—have died.
182: And wiped away is all the substance that is on the face of the ground, from man unto beast, unto creeping thing, and unto fowl of the heavens; yea, they are wiped away from the earth, and only Noah is left, and those who are with him in the ark;
184: And God remembereth Noah, and every living thing, and all the cattle which are with him in the ark, and God causeth a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters subside,
185: and closed are the fountains of the deep and the net-work of the heavens, and restrained is the shower from the heavens.
186: And turn back do the waters from off the earth, going on and returning; and the waters are lacking at the end of a hundred and fifty days.
187: And the ark resteth, in the seventh month, in the seventeenth day of the month, on mountains of Ararat;
188: and the waters have been going and becoming lacking till the tenth month; in the tenth month, on the first of the month, appeared the heads of the mountains.
189: And it cometh to pass, at the end of forty days, that Noah openeth the window of the ark which he made,
190: and he sendeth forth the raven, and it goeth out, going out and turning back till the drying of the waters from off the earth.
191: And he sendeth forth the dove from him to see whether the waters have been lightened from off the face of the ground,
192: and the dove hath not found rest for the sole of her foot, and she turneth back unto him, unto the ark, for waters are on the face of all the earth, and he putteth out his hand, and taketh her, and bringeth her in unto him, unto the ark.
193: And he stayeth yet other seven days, and addeth to send forth the dove from the ark;
194: and the dove cometh in unto him at even-time, and lo, an olive leaf torn off in her mouth; and Noah knoweth that the waters have been lightened from off the earth.
195: And he stayeth yet other seven days, and sendeth forth the dove, and it added not to turn back unto him any more.
196: And it cometh to pass in the six hundredth and first year, in the first month, in the first of the month, the waters have been dried from off the earth; and Noah turneth aside the covering of the ark, and looketh, and lo, the face of the ground hath been dried.
197: And in the second month, in the seven and twentieth day of the month, the earth hath become dry.
198: And God speaketh unto Noah, saying, ‘Go out from the ark, thou, and thy wife, and thy sons, and thy sons’ wives with thee;
200: and they have teemed in the earth, and been fruitful, and have multiplied on the earth.’
202: every beast, every creeping thing, and every fowl; every creeping thing on the earth, after their families, have gone out from the ark.
203: And Noah buildeth an altar to Jehovah, and taketh of every clean beast, and of every clean fowl, and causeth burnt-offerings to ascend on the altar;
204: and Jehovah smelleth the sweet fragrance, and Jehovah saith unto His heart, ‘I continue not to disesteem any more the ground because of man, though the imagination of the heart of man is evil from his youth; and I continue not to smite any more all living, as I have done;
205: during all days of the earth, seed-time and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night, do not cease.’
207: and your fear and your dread is on every beast of the earth, and on every fowl of the heavens, on all that creepeth on the ground, and on all fishes of the sea—into your hand they have been given.
210: ‘And only your blood for your lives do I require; from the hand of every living thing I require it, and from the hand of man, from the hand of every man’s brother I require the life of man;
211: whoso sheddeth man’s blood, by man is his blood shed: for in the image of God hath He made man.
214: ‘And I, lo, I am establishing My covenant with you, and with your seed after you,
216: And I have established My covenant with you, and all flesh is not any more cut off by waters of a deluge, and there is not any more a deluge to destroy the earth.’
217: And God saith, ‘This is a token of the covenant which I am giving between Me and you, and every living creature that is with you, to generations age-during;
218: My bow I have given in the cloud, and it hath been for a token of a covenant between Me and the earth;
220: and I have remembered My covenant which is between Me and you, and every living creature among all flesh, and the waters become no more a deluge to destroy all flesh;
221: and the bow hath been in the cloud, and I have seen it—to remember the covenant age-during between God and every living creature among all flesh which is on the earth.’
223: And the sons of Noah who are going out of the ark are Shem, and Ham, and Japheth; and Ham is father of Canaan.
224: These three are sons of Noah, and from these hath all the earth been overspread.
225: And Noah remaineth a man of the ground, and planteth a vineyard,
226: and drinketh of the wine, and is drunken, and uncovereth himself in the midst of the tent.
227: And Ham, father of Canaan, seeth the nakedness of his father, and declareth to his two brethren without.
228: And Shem taketh—Japheth also—the garment, and they place on the shoulder of them both, and go backward, and cover the nakedness of their father; and their faces are backward, and their father’s nakedness they have not seen.
229: And Noah awaketh from his wine, and knoweth that which his young son hath done to him,
230: and saith: ‘Cursed is Canaan, Servant of servants he is to his brethren.’
231: And he saith: ‘Blessed of Jehovah my God is Shem, And Canaan is servant to him.
232: God doth give beauty to Japheth, And he dwelleth in tents of Shem, And Canaan is servant to him.’
236: Sons of Japheth are Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, and Javan, and Tubal, and Meshech, and Tiras.
237: And sons of Gomer are Ashkenaz, and Riphath, and Togarmah.
238: And sons of Javan are Elishah, and Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
239: By these have the isles of the nations been parted in their lands, each by his tongue, by their families, in their nations.
240: And sons of Ham are Cush, and Mitzraim, and Phut, and Canaan.
241: And sons of Cush are Seba, and Havilah, and Sabtah, and Raamah, and Sabtechah; and sons of Raamah are Sheba and Dedan.
243: he hath begun to be a hero in the land; he hath been a hero in hunting before Jehovah; therefore it is said, ‘As Nimrod the hero in hunting before Jehovah.’
244: And the first part of his kingdom is Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar;
245: from that land he hath gone out to Asshur, and buildeth Nineveh, even the broad places of the city, and Calah,
246: and Resen, between Nineveh and Calah; it is the great city.
247: And Mitzraim hath begotten the Ludim, and the Anamim, and the Lehabim, and the Naphtuhim,
248: and the Pathrusim, and the Casluhim, (whence have come out Philistim,) and the Caphtorim.
249: And Canaan hath begotten Sidon his first-born, and Heth,
250: and the Jebusite, and the Amorite, and the Girgashite,
251: and the Hivite, and the Arkite, and the Sinite,
252: and the Arvadite, and the Zemarite, and the Hamathite; and afterwards have the families of the Canaanite been scattered.
253: And the border of the Canaanite is from Sidon, in thy coming towards Gerar, unto Gaza; in thy coming towards Sodom, and Gomorrah, and Admah, and Zeboim, unto Lasha.
254: These are sons of Ham, by their families, by their tongues, in their lands, in their nations.
255: As to Shem, father of all sons of Eber, brother of Japheth the elder, he hath also begotten:
256: Sons of Shem are Elam, and Asshur, and Arphaxad, and Lud, and Aram.
257: And sons of Aram are Uz, and Hul, and Gether, and Mash.
258: And Arphaxad hath begotten Salah, and Salah hath begotten Eber.
259: And to Eber have two sons been born; the name of the one is Peleg (for in his days hath the earth been divided,) and his brother’s name is Joktan.
260: And Joktan hath begotten Almodad, and Sheleph, and Hazarmaveth, and Jerah,
261: and Hadoram, and Uzal, and Diklah,
262: and Obal, and Abimael, and Sheba,
263: and Ophir, and Havilah, and Jobab; all these are sons of Joktan;

1896: and he taketh six hundred chosen chariots, even all the chariots of Egypt, and captains over them all;
1898: and the Egyptians pursue after them, and all the chariot horses of Pharaoh, and his horsemen, and his force, overtake them, encamping by the sea, by Pi-Hahiroth, before Baal-Zephon.
1900: And they say unto Moses, ‘Because there are no graves in Egypt, hast thou taken us away to die in a wilderness? what is this thou hast done to us—to bring us out from Egypt?
1903: Jehovah doth fight for you, and ye keep silent.’
1904: And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ‘What? thou criest unto Me—speak unto the sons of Israel, and they journey;
1906: ‘And I—lo, I am strengthening the heart of the Egyptians, and they go in after them, and I am honoured on Pharaoh, and on all his force, on his chariots, and on his horsemen;
1908: And the messenger of God, who is going before the camp of Israel, journeyeth and goeth at their rear; and the pillar of the cloud journeyeth from their front, and standeth at their rear,
1909: and cometh in between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Israel, and the cloud and the darkness are, and he enlighteneth the night, and the one hath not drawn near unto the other all the night.
1913: and it cometh to pass, in the morning watch, that Jehovah looketh unto the camp of the Egyptians through the pillar of fire and of the cloud, and troubleth the camp of the Egyptians,
1914: and turneth aside the wheels of their chariots, and they lead them with difficulty, and the Egyptians say, ‘Let us flee from the face of Israel, for Jehovah is fighting for them against the Egyptians.’
1916: And Moses stretcheth out his hand towards the sea, and the sea turneth back, at the turning of the morning, to its perennial flow, and the Egyptians are fleeing at its coming, and Jehovah shaketh off the Egyptians in the midst of the sea,
1920: and Israel seeth the great hand with which Jehovah hath wrought against the Egyptians, and the people fear Jehovah, and remain stedfast in Jehovah, and in Moses His servant.
1921: Then singeth Moses and the sons of Israel this song to Jehovah, and they speak, saying:—‘I sing to Jehovah, For triumphing He hath triumphed; The horse and its rider He hath thrown into the sea.
1922: My strength and song is JAH, And He is become my salvation: This is my God, and I glorify Him; God of my father, and I exalt Him.
1924: Chariots of Pharaoh and his force He hath cast into the sea; And the choice of his captains Have sunk in the Red Sea!
1925: The depths do cover them; They went down into the depths as a stone.
1926: Thy right hand, O Jehovah, Is become honourable in power; Thy right hand, O Jehovah, Doth crush an enemy.
1927: And in the abundance of Thine excellency Thou throwest down Thy withstanders, Thou sendest forth Thy wrath—It consumeth them as stubble.
1928: And by the spirit of Thine anger Have waters been heaped together; Stood as a heap have flowings; Congealed have been depths In the heart of a sea.
1929: The enemy said, I pursue, I overtake; I apportion spoil; Filled is my soul with them; I draw out my sword; My hand destroyeth them:—
1930: Thou hast blown with Thy wind The sea hath covered them; They sank as lead in mighty waters.
1931: Who is like Thee among the gods, O Jehovah? Who is like Thee—honourable in holiness—Fearful in praises—doing wonders?
1933: Thou hast led forth in Thy kindness The people whom Thou hast redeemed. Thou hast led on in Thy strength Unto Thy holy habitation.
1934: Peoples have heard, they are troubled; Pain hath seized inhabitants of Philistia.
1935: Then have chiefs of Edom been troubled: Mighty ones of Moab—Trembling doth seize them! Melted have all inhabitants of Canaan!
1936: Fall on them doth terror and dread; By the greatness of Thine arm They are still as a stone, Till Thy people pass over, O Jehovah; Till the people pass over Whom Thou hast purchased.
1937: Thou dost bring them in, And dost plant them In a mountain of Thine inheritance, A fixed place for Thy dwelling Thou hast made, O Jehovah; A sanctuary, O Lord, Thy hands have established;
1938: Jehovah reigneth—to the age, and for ever!’
1940: And Miriam the inspired one, sister of Aaron, taketh the timbrel in her hand, and all the women go out after her, with timbrels and with choruses;
1943: and they come in to Marah, and have not been able to drink the waters of Marah, for they are bitter; therefore hath one called its name Marah.
1944: And the people murmur against Moses, saying, ‘What do we drink?’
1945: and he crieth unto Jehovah, and Jehovah sheweth him a tree, and he casteth unto the waters, and the waters become sweet. There He hath made for them a statute, and an ordinance, and there He hath tried them,
1946: and He saith, ‘If thou dost really hearken to the voice of Jehovah thy God, and dost that which is right in His eyes, and hast hearkened to His commands, and kept all His statutes: none of the sickness which I laid on the Egyptians do I lay on thee, for I, Jehovah, am healing thee.
1947: And they come to Elim, and there are twelve fountains of water, and seventy palm trees; and they encamp there by the waters.
1948: And they journey from Elim, and all the company of the sons of Israel come in unto the wilderness of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month of their going out from the land of Egypt.
1950: and the sons of Israel say unto them, ‘Oh that we had died by the hand of Jehovah in the land of Egypt, in our sitting by the flesh-pot, in our eating bread to satiety—for ye have brought us out unto this wilderness to put all this assembly to death with hunger.’
1951: And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ‘Lo, I am raining to you bread from the heavens—and the people have gone out and gathered the matter of a day in its day—so that I try them whether they walk in My law, or not;
1954: and morning—and ye have seen the honour of Jehovah, in His hearing your murmurings against Jehovah, and what are we, that ye murmur against us?’
1955: And Moses saith, ‘In Jehovah’s giving to you in the evening flesh to eat, and bread in the morning to satiety—in Jehovah’s hearing your murmurings, which ye are murmuring against Him, and what are we? your murmurings are not against us, but against Jehovah.’
1960: And it cometh to pass in the evening, that the quail cometh up, and covereth the camp, and in the morning there hath been the lying of dew round about the camp,
1961: and the lying of the dew goeth up, and lo, on the face of the wilderness a thin, bare thing, thin as hoar-frost on the earth.
1963: This is the thing which Jehovah hath commanded: Gather of it each according to his eating, an omer for a poll; and the number of your persons, take ye each for those in his tent.’
1964: And the sons of Israel do so, and they gather, he who is gathering much, and he who is gathering little;
1965: and they measure with an omer, and he who is gathering much hath nothing over, and he who is gathering little hath no lack, each according to his eating they have gathered.
1967: and they have not hearkened unto Moses, and some of them do leave of it till morning, and it bringeth up worms and stinketh; and Moses is wroth with them.
1968: And they gather it morning by morning, each according to his eating; when the sun hath been warm, then it hath melted.
1969: And it cometh to pass on the sixth day, they have gathered a second bread, two omers for one, and all the princes of the company come in, and declare to Moses.
1970: And he saith unto them, ‘It is that which Jehovah hath spoken of; a rest—a holy sabbath to Jehovah—is to-morrow; that which ye bake, bake; and that which ye boil, boil; and all that is over, let rest for yourselves in charge till the morning.’
1971: And they let it rest until the morning, as Moses hath commanded, and it hath not stank, and a worm hath not been in it.
1978: and the house of Israel call its name Manna, and it is as coriander seed, white; and its taste is as a cake with honey.
1981: as Jehovah hath given commandment unto Moses, so doth Aaron let it rest before the Testimony, for a charge.
1982: And the sons of Israel have eaten the manna forty years, until their coming in unto the land to be inhabited; the manna they have eaten till their coming in unto the extremity of the land of Canaan.
1984: And all the company of the sons of Israel journey from the wilderness of Sin, on their journeyings, by the command of Jehovah, and encamp in Rephidim, and there is no water for the people to drink;
1986: and the people thirst there for water, and the people murmur against Moses, and say, ‘Why is this?—thou hast brought us up out of Egypt, to put us to death, also our sons and our cattle, with thirst.’
1987: And Moses crieth to Jehovah, saying, ‘What do I to this people? yet a little, and they have stoned me.’
1989: Lo, I am standing before thee there on the rock in Horeb, and thou hast smitten on the rock, and waters have come out from it, and the people have drunk.’ And Moses doth so before the eyes of the elders of Israel,
1990: and he calleth the name of the place Massah, and Meribah, because of the ‘strife’ of the sons of Israel, and because of their ‘trying’ Jehovah, saying, ‘Is Jehovah in our midst or not?’
1991: And Amalek cometh, and fighteth with Israel in Rephidim,
1992: and Moses saith unto Joshua, ‘Choose for us men, and go out, fight with Amalek: to-morrow I am standing on the top of the hill, and the rod of God in my hand.’
1993: And Joshua doth as Moses hath said to him, to fight with Amalek, and Moses, Aaron, and Hur, have gone up to the top of the height;
1996: and Joshua weakeneth Amalek and his people by the mouth of the sword.
1997: And Jehovah saith unto Moses, ‘Write this, a memorial in a Book, and set it in the ears of Joshua, that I do utterly wipe away the remembrance of Amalek from under the heavens;’
